text:
Alex Chu: Heads-up — invoice preview shows ~2% token inflation for a subset of EU tenants when sampling is on. Seen under Billing > Previews.
Maria Gonzales: Hmm. Is that the route-level sampling flag we flipped last Thursday? :thinking_face:
Alex Chu: Looks correlated by time. Spike starts right after the sampling rollout to chat_stream routes around 08:12 UTC.
Ben Platform: Confirming — edge sampler emits sampled events with sample_rate metadata. The downstream aggregator was supposed to scale by 1/sample_rate but I found an older codepath that treats sample_rate as an integer percentage (e.g., 5 instead of 0.05).
Samir Patel: Oof. That would multiply tokens by 20x for 5% samples. Can you paste the reducer snippet?
Ben Platform: Sure — current code: ```js
// aggregator.js
const est = events.reduce((acc, e) => acc + e.tokens * (1 / e.sample_rate), 0)
```
Ben Platform: Problem is some proxies send sample_rate=5 (meaning 5%) while the canonical schema expects 0.05.
Alex Chu: So we have mixed conventions across proxies. Where's contract defined? I thought metering.v1.ingest has schema.sample_rate: number (fraction).
Maria Gonzales: That was the plan but the old proxy (edge-v1) still emits percent to be compact. We didn't add validation in the gateway, my bad.
Julie (ops): For quick mitigation: can we add a corrective transform in the preview pipeline that treats values >1 as percentages and divides by 100? That avoids a backfill.
Samir Patel: Yes, but preview vs final invoice paths diverge — preview uses the preview-aggregator lambda while billing uses the ledger-compiler. We need both patched or else previews will disagree with final invoices.
Ben Platform: Agreed. My vote: patch gateway to normalize sample_rate (accept both, always store fraction) and add a one-off compensating transform in preview to avoid alert fatigue. Then deploy ledger-compiler patch next release.
Alex Chu: Can we also add telemetry / an alert when sample_rate > 1? Like a RATE_LIMIT on unusual schema values so we catch other mismatches before they affect previews.
Maria Gonzales: +1. Also propose a console UX tweak: show a per-route sampling legend on the Billing preview page and a hover tooltip that explains how previews estimate tokens when sampling is enabled.
Julie (ops): For rollout: create a canary rule to enable gateway normalization only for internal tenants and EU-1. If all clear for 24h, we flip globally.
metering-bot: deploy-bot: canary deploy gateway-normalize-sampler to eu-1 at 2026-03-20T11:05:12Z :rocket:
Samir Patel: After we normalize, we should re-run the preview recompute for affected tenants (hourly window) to update preview caches. I can add a job to recompute previews for tenants with preview_delta > 0.5%.
Ben Platform: I'll open the PR for gateway validation + ledger-compiler fix. Tagging @Maria for console tooltip copy.
Maria Gonzales: I'll draft the tooltip: "When sampling is enabled, token counts are estimated by scaling sampled events. If proxies send sample_rate as percent, the system normalizes to a fraction." Will post in #docs-review.
Alex Chu: Thanks all. Action items: Ben PR, Samir recompute job, Maria tooltip, Julie coordinate canary. If anyone spots tenants with big invoice deltas ping me.
Julie (ops): Noted. I'll monitor invoice-preview-alerts and mute noisy channel until we have patched-transform in preview.
Alex Chu: Adding a follow-up: we should consider adding deterministic request fingerprinting at the router so duplicate events from retries/syncs can be deduped before sampling compensation inflates counts.
Ben Platform: Agreed — follow-up ticket created: INF-4319 "router deterministic fingerprint for metering dedupe". I'll link it to the PR.
Alex Chu: Good. Closing the loop here, will update when canary finishes. :thumbsup:"
